title: I Let the Bowling-Alley Shoe Timer Hit the League Captain Who Wrote It

parts.text: I opened lane twelve at 6:12 p.m. and the rental counter already had a tower of size-10s tagged LEAGUE HOLD. The timer the captain laminated said: RENTAL SHOES RETURN AT GAME END. NO HOLDS PAST THE BUZZER. I was twenty-six, desk lead, holding a birthday kid whose only remaining tens were in that tower. Captain Reese said, "League shoes don't buzz." I pointed at his own timer. He grinned. "Captains are the house." I photographed the tags, the timer, and the kid's ticket. Then I scanned every hold back into inventory when the buzzer hit 6:30. At 6:31 the manager asked why Reese's name was on a shoe-overtime report.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see the league hold tower scanned back at the buzzer Reese wrote.

social.video_title: League holds don't beat the shoe buzzer — Part 1/2
social.description: Birthday kid, a captain's tower of tens, and a timer he laminated. I scanned them back. Would you have waited?

parts.text: Reese called it tradition until the birthday invoice showed a wait. I printed the report, the timer, and the photo. We issued the kid new tens. Reese bowled in house socks and told the league the timer was always about optics. Optics is a word captains use when a scan exists. Rental policy now has a second line: LEAGUE IS NOT A HOLD. I keep tens on a labeled rack. Reese brings his own. The buzzer sounds like it finally got the memo.

social.video_title: League is not a shoe hold — Part 2/2
social.description: Overtime report, house socks, and a second line on the timer. Was the birthday ever the house?
